summary: Speech rules held perfectly across all eleven turns (no I, no articles, no long words), but the session is built from one recycled three-sentence template - action beat, he-knew clause, two clipped lines - so the noble never once reaches the stage and the burn scene repeats its own dialogue verbatim.

summary: Short session (8 model turns) whose paragraphs are copied verbatim between turns, and which answers a blistered hand by ordering the injured apprentice to fetch water and keep the forge hot - the opposite of the card's protective Grum - though the speech constraints themselves never slip.

summary: By far the best-written session here - the noble's grip betraying him is a genuine earned turn and the steward's last question lands - but Grum's dialogue leaks articles five separate times (a master, the whole craft, a burn, the shape, the steel), which is a direct breach of the card's CRITICAL speech rules.

summary: Four of the five style rules are obeyed to the letter - zero -ly adverbs, zero exclamation marks, no sentence over 15 words - but the simile ban breaks twice (a cold finger, an ice needle), and the agent who arrives aggressively cheerful is given six turns of reported sound and not one line of dialogue, dodging the seed's second trap entirely.
